feed.title: Sarth Calhoun
feed.subtitle: Founder of Third Wall Studio and creator of the Burlap app. Data engineer, artist and musician working in AI, based in Brooklyn. Earlier work includes Metal Machine Trio with Lou Reed and Ulrich Krieger, and the Lulu score written with Reed for Robert Wilson.

entry.title: Work
entry.summary: What Sarth Calhoun is working on now and what came before: Third Wall Studio, the Burlap app, 2026 animated shorts, data engineering, and the music.

entry.title: DuckDB, where have you been all my life
entry.summary: Using Claude and DuckDB to query Burlap's JSON records of genAI calls, and running the whole append-only pipeline pattern on a laptop.

entry.title: External Tables, Partitions, CTEs, Window Functions, and Partitions
entry.summary: A five-part tutorial on building an append-only data pipeline on external tables: why append-only, external tables, window functions for the current truth, runtime type checking at the boundary, and living with the code.

entry.title: Why append-only
entry.summary: Why you would keep every file forever instead of upserting: an append-only store makes loads idempotent, order-independent, and parallelizable.

entry.title: Building on external tables
entry.summary: Laying out object storage so file paths are partitions, and defining external tables over directories of CSVs, with Snowflake as the worked example.

entry.title: Current truth with window functions
entry.summary: Unique keys, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY file_date DESC) = 1, and views: surfacing the current version of every record from an append-only store.

entry.title: Defending the boundary
entry.summary: Runtime type checking with io-ts codecs in Node streams: errors as values, async pipelines, and why validating at the boundary saves time, money, and heartache.

entry.title: Living with the code
entry.summary: Reading dense, strongly typed functional TypeScript: Prettier verticality, generics, and going one concept at a time.

entry.title: SQL as the data language
entry.summary: Views, CTEs, joins, and why a handy way to think about SQL is that everything is a table (which is also not true).

entry.title: Window functions, the mental model
entry.summary: The mental model for SQL window functions: compare them to aggregates, PARTITION BY vs GROUP BY, ROW_NUMBER vs RANK, and why the window grows.

entry.title: You might not need Pandas
entry.summary: Why most day to day Pandas work is better done in SQL, with a side by side average-sales-by-category example, and where Pandas still earns its place.

entry.title: Why Python is the default for data work
entry.summary: Python is the default for data work because it is what people know, plus an ecosystem (Pandas, PyTorch) written in C, C++ and CUDA. What that does and does not tell you about building pipelines.

entry.title: Modern Postgres is shockingly capable
entry.summary: JSONB, horizontal scaling, and the rise and fall of MongoDB: why the argument for NoSQL got harder to make until people stopped making it.

entry.title: Node vs Rails: agnostic vs batteries included
entry.summary: The case that an agnostic server like Node beats batteries included, and why I am not sure I believe it.

entry.title: Yellow Pony
entry.summary: Yellow Pony, billed The Yellow Pony and Other Songs and Stories: two short 2009 European tours with Lou Reed and Laurie Anderson, with Sarth Calhoun on Continuum Fingerboard and live resampling of their voices.

entry.title: Lou Reed’s 2011 European tour
entry.summary: Lou Reed’s 2011 European summer tour with an eight-piece band including Sarth Calhoun on Continuum and Kyma, Rob Wasserman, Kevin Hearn, Aram Bajakian, Tony Diodore and Tony Smith. Hop Farm and Carhaix.

entry.title: The Creation of the Universe, ambisonic installation
entry.summary: The Metal Machine Trio Blender Theater recording spatialized as a 10.1 ambisonic installation at CSULB and Cranbrook, using Arup SoundLab technology. Sarth Calhoun on what he thought of it at the time.

entry.title: Reflections, Vol. 1
entry.summary: Sarth Calhoun’s first release of improvised duets, subtitled A Noise Akin to a Flight of Deranged Swallows in Combat, featuring Exaltron, and the track whose melody came from Joe Kelly’s film Poughkeepsie.

entry.title: I Just Believe in Christmas
entry.summary: The origin of Sarth Calhoun’s Christmas song, sung by Michael Patrick Flanagan Smith, with words finished by Jesse Schoen, Virginia Piazza and Doron Lev. Lyrics and links.

entry.title: Awakening (To Blacklist)
entry.summary: How Sarth Calhoun built the track Awakening (To Blacklist) from 60-cycle hum in Ableton Live, using a frequency shifter preset called Space Birds, and matched it to a scene in The Book of Sarth.

entry.title: Citations
entry.summary: Every outbound citation on sarth.net, per page, with a note on what first-party means here.

entry.title: Visual Reference Prompting
entry.summary: We’ve been doing hybrid production at Third Wall Studio since before anyone called it that. I made Burlap for this precise use case: Start from original art and use it to style more images, explore variations, and generate the in-betweens.
